items.title: “Does Meta think we can’t read?” Meta abandons sketchy commercial terms update.
items.excerpt: Meta withdrew its planned commercial terms update and won't force Facebook page owners to allow AI training on linked content. The terms were due to take effect Nov 20 and were already under a UK CMA probe and court challenges in Norway and Brazil.

items.title: AP sources: Staff at U.S. center for AI safety are reporting to the White House, raising independence concerns
items.excerpt: Two former officials told AP that staff at the Commerce Department's AI standards center (CAISI) were asked to informally report to a White House office. The center has no permanent leader and has stopped publishing research. The White House pointed to Trump's Super Intelligence Force and a PCAST report it commissioned.

items.title: Russia and US seek to block plan for binding rules on autonomous weapons
items.excerpt: Russia and the US are seeking to block a plan for a legally binding instrument on lethal autonomous weapons ahead of a UN conference this month, seen as a key moment after years of talks on filling the governance gap for AI weapons systems.

items.title: 3 allegedly used AI to steal some $129 million from companies by impersonating executives and lawyers
items.excerpt: Federal prosecutors indicted three people accused of using AI-cloned voices and images of corporate executives and attorneys to convince employees to wire about $129 million. Off-list outlet used because AP and Courthouse News were blocked; DOJ indictment is the primary event.

items.title: 中, AI 악용·선정적 숏폼 드라마 연말까지 집중단속
items.excerpt: 중국 국가광파전시총국(광전총국)이 AI를 이용한 저질·선정적 숏폼 드라마에 대해 12월 31일까지 특별단속에 나선다. 아동 유해물, 선정성, 저작권 침해 등이 대상이며 올해만 7만5천 편이 퇴출됐다.

items.title: Foster bill would bolster tech use to monitor AI financial risks
items.excerpt: Rep. Bill Foster (D-Ill.) introduced legislation Thursday to help financial regulators use technology to spot financial stress turbocharged by AI and around-the-clock payment systems.

items.title: Singapore authorities urge strict limits on AI agent autonomy, access to personal accounts
items.excerpt: An advisory issued Nov 6 by Singapore's Cyber Security Agency, GovTech and IMDA tells consumers to connect only necessary apps to personal AI agents, restrict sensitive accounts and require permission before deleting or sharing files; it follows the Singapore launch of Meta Muse.

items.title: Delaware's 'Artificial Intelligence Company' proposal to be investigated; Comer sends Gov. Matt Meyer letter
items.excerpt: House Oversight Chairman James Comer is investigating Delaware's effort to create a new corporate entity, the Artificial Intelligence Company, that AI agents could run without human executives, in a letter to Gov. Matt Meyer. Follow-up to the 10-28 Delaware plan card: new = formal congressional letter.

items.title: Claude now watermarks text from older models, with no opt-out
items.excerpt: Anthropic has been adding an invisible watermark to text from Claude Mythos 5, Opus 4.7 and Sonnet 4.6 since Nov 3, with older models following Nov 16; customers cannot turn it off. Reports tie the move to EU AI Act transparency (Article 50) obligations.

items.title: China stalls Nvidia H200 imports to boost domestic AI chips
items.excerpt: About 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips are piled up in Hong Kong because Beijing has not approved large-scale imports, despite US export approval; the slow-walk aims to protect China's domestic chip industry and has pushed up gray-market prices.

items.title: Wavestone joins European Commission consortium to assess cyber risks of advanced AI models
items.excerpt: The European Commission's AI Office selected a Capgemini-led consortium with Wavestone and France's LNE to assess and mitigate cyber risks from advanced general-purpose AI models under the EU AI Act's AI Safety programme.

items.title: State to scrap ticketless AI parking fines following errors
items.excerpt: The South Australian government will overhaul council use of AI-assisted camera cars, scrapping ticketless parking fines that arrive by mail weeks later after a high rate of challenged fines were withdrawn.

items.title: ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base: Baidu's New Open-Weight Model May Not Be Used in the EU
items.excerpt: Baidu's new 280-billion-parameter open-weight model ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base may not be used in the EU, the UK or South Korea under its license terms, a regulatory geofence on AI rules.

items.title: 과기정통부·KISA, '에이전틱 AI 제로트러스트 안내서' 발간
items.excerpt: 과기정통부와 KISA가 AI 에이전트가 부여받은 권한을 넘어 자율 행동하거나 외부 입력으로 잘못된 명령을 수행하는 위협에 대응하는 '에이전틱 AI 제로트러스트 안내서'를 발간했다.

items.title: Japan launches emergency cybersecurity package after wave of attacks
items.excerpt: PM Sanae Takaichi's government adopted a ¥10 billion emergency cyber package that includes AI-based countermeasures, citing the need to keep up with 'the speed of cyberattacks in the AI era' after a Chinese AI hacking tool was linked to breaches of Japanese firms.

items.title: Europe's AI Ambitions Meet the Data Center Backlash
items.excerpt: Protests are sweeping Europe against AI data center expansion, with growing calls for a moratorium over environmental and social costs as the EU pushes AI gigafactories.

items.title: Character.ai sale contract omits 40 attorneys general's user data conditions
items.excerpt: Court sale filings for Character.ai assets outside Disney's license offer as-is terms and a Dec 17 exit date but omit the user-data privacy conditions 40 state attorneys general sought.

items.title: Commission rights method flags AI credit scoring and insurance pricing
items.excerpt: An EU-funded fundamental-rights impact assessment method gives AI deployers a 4-level likelihood/severity scale per right; AI Act deployer checks begin Dec 2, 2027.
